cursor.standing: PROVED — THE BUILD GATE HOLDS THE PROVEME EXIT. transitions.emit now runs the build_inspector on the component at a journaled crossing's own address before any forward move out of PROVEME, and refuses on red BEFORE anything is written (build_inspector filed edge (a), landed). Wired at the emit-chokepoint because the clearance gate wraps emit — this is the one door, so 'CC runs it by discipline' is retired for every journaled promotion. Kick-backs out of PROVEME are never gated (retreat on red is correct); an unaddressed exit is a string calculation (no journal, no jurisdiction); an address the census cannot see is REFUSED with its growth path named, never waved through (Law 8 — no side door). A clean exit journals its gate verdict in the crossing record (build_gate field). Live-fired on the real tree: bus's promotion REFUSED by silent_device, history untouched. Proven 17/17 (5 new teeth) under the tester's netns seal; inspector/orient/clearance/append-door proofs all green beside it.

window.standing: DE-BRITTLED test_transitions.py — the live-ticket parse tooth no longer pins harbor-master's cursor to a snapshot value (it read BUILDME, then broke when the ticket legitimately advanced to PROVED as its journey view landed). Now it asserts INVARIANTS over the real on-disk ticket: node_class/version, the declared path is byte-equal to the registered v1 table (a conformance/drift check — strictly stronger than guessing one stage), and the cursor parsed to SOME real stage on that path. A proof that pins a legitimately-moving value re-derives noise (Law 1). transitions.py itself unchanged — only the proof hardened; re-sealed under a real netns.

PROVED — WHAT RIDES ALONG IS A CARRIER. Callback gained `carry`: an optional (context) -> dict evaluated at FIRE time, merged over the static `body`, so a gate-watching callback can send the thing that crossed in whatever form the receiver can process. Akien 2026-07-25: 'a gate callback can say call dave back with "ticket detected at {gatename} as {ticket}" — whatever the callback can process in that location', and the payload need not be an artifact at all (the inference proxy's loop-count-over-N). Carriage is a CALLABLE, never a named kind — the same anti-reification the trigger already carries, one file up. by_pointer (the Law 6 default: only the address leaves) / by_copy (deep, so the receiver cannot reach back) / by_text (a format template) ship because they have consumers; a fourth carriage is a fourth function, not a schema change. Law 6 moves to the AUTHOR: sending owned data is now an explicit, greppable choice made in the owning device, exactly where the trigger's closure already puts it. A carrier that raises does NOT swallow the poke — it lands carrying carry_failed (Law 7, Akien's no-silent-failure rule). shim._fire posts cb.payload(context), so the bus's one producer now carries the moment, not the declaration.
window.note: The proof went red only in the SUITE (2 pokes, not 1) — the bus is durable via db_domain, so counting a live channel pinned a moving value. Fixed to the bus's own ephemeral-table pattern (nonce table + teardown); verified by running it twice.

window.standing: PROVED — A POKE PER CROSSING, NOT PER PULSE. Akien: 'so we need an anti-bounce?' Measured yes: on_pulse fired on the LEVEL, so a trigger parked true (a CPU at 91%) poked every pulse forever — the flood rackmount.py:129 filed as 'wants edge-detection' and left. Now the default is one poke at the crossing false->true, re-arming when the line is recrossed; Callback.while_true opts back into per-pulse for the watch that means 'keep telling me while this holds'. The DECLARATION is on the frozen Callback, the MEMORY is on the shim (_was_true, keyed by Callback.identity = to/channel/why) — the same declare/evaluate split the trigger already has, and the reason crossing-detection cannot live in callback.py. A raising trigger is remembered as NEITHER side of the line, so a swallowed error never also swallows the next real poke (Law 7); a vanished or re-established watch is forgotten rather than suppressed by stale memory; every held poke now says WHICH kind of held it is.
window.note: Named 'crossing', not 'edge' — 'filed edge' is already spent in this codebase on an open design question, and 'crossing' is already native (diagnostic.py's 'a boundary crossing', rackmount's {'crossed': value}). Coinage-by-selection, flagged for ratify. CHATTER (a value flapping across the line) is NOT cured by this and is deliberately NOT built — damping needs a measured width, and a wrong width silently eats real crossings. Filed with its opening condition on CairnCommons/tickets/bus-completion.json.

window.standing: PROVED — THE CROSSING NOW SAYS WHERE THE BOAT STANDS. transitions.emit derives `standing` from the target it just landed on, instead of leaving it to every caller to remember. Found by the append door's new shape gate (cairn/charter/projector.py), which refused emit's record on its first run: from/to/workflow/direction and no `standing` — the one field harbor_master's register reads to place a boat, so every such record would have been permanently unreadable. Measured: zero emit-shaped records existed in any live history, so nothing malformed was ever written; the gate caught it while it was still cheap. A caller may still override with a richer line through journal_extra — the default is a floor, not a ceiling. Proven 11/11 (2 new); full suite 31/31 green.
